root_idea.summary: The root centers on softness, yieldingness, and freedom from rigidity or strain, with a related classical association of lightness or shallowness of mind.
root_idea.development: Its semantic range develops from physical softness and looseness to slackening or letting down, gentle and unimpeded running or wind, ease and abundance of circumstances, and the slowing or postponement of an action or event.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic noun citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression at 38:36, the wind is described as running at command; the usage conveys gentleness and ease of movement, with traditional interpretations also emphasizing speed without resistance or opposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become soft, yielding, flaccid, slack, uncompact, fragile, brittle, or easily broken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A basic intransitive verbal use, applied to things that lose firmness or compactness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of life or a person's circumstances, to become ample, unstraitened, or plentiful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to means or circumstances of life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mixing of one thing with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II verbal-noun construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make distant or remote, or to become distant from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or transitive Form III use expressing separation or remoteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to be near bringing forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form III usage referring to approaching childbirth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make soft, yielding, lax, slack, fragile, or easily broken; to relax or loosen something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of ties, bonds, shackles, ropes, reins, and similar things; the intensive or comparative expression أَشَدُّ إِرْخَاءً means more or most relaxing, slackening, or loosening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To let down, lower, or allow to hang loosely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a veil, curtain, clothing, or a similar hanging object or portion of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give ease, relief, delay, or ample scope; to leave someone free to manage an affair as they please.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These figurative uses arise from loosening a restraint, tether, or difficulty; loosening one's turban can likewise express becoming secure or at ease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, for the parts on either side of the tail to relax or gape at parturition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage associated with giving birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode of running that is easy or gentle and exceeds ordinary trotting, ranging from unimpetuous running to very fast running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of horses and other riding animals; it can also mean letting an animal follow its own eager desire in running without tiring it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slacken, flag, or become remiss or languid in running, an affair, or the accomplishment of a need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a runner, an affair, or a person pursuing an objective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw back, hold back, or hang back from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI use with عن expressing withdrawal or holding back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become slow, late, delayed, or protracted; to leave an interval or ample time for action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of rain, time, or an affair; تَرَاخٍ may denote an interval, extension, or remoteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become relaxed, slack, or loosely pendent; to hang down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a veil, curtain, garment, hair, or a lock of hair, and of similar things that hang loosely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, for the parts on either side of the tail to relax or gape at parturition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical construction referring to the onset of giving birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak or slack in one's opinion after having been strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to firmness of judgment or resolve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's circumstances to become good, ample, or unstraitened after difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes improvement into a state of ease or plenty after prior constraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, yielding, flaccid, flabby, lax, uncompact, fragile, brittle, friable, or easily broken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The forms differ by accepted vocalization or dialect; the adjective may be applied to things of any kind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Easy, gentle, moderate, or leisurely in pace; tractable or easy to lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a horse or mare, including the construction رِخْوُ العِنَانِ, easy to control by the reins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A continuant or lax letter in which the sound runs on rather than being stopped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical phonetic use for the class of letters distinguished from the stops and intermediate letters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Softness, yieldingness, flaccidity, laxity, or looseness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or abstract noun denoting the state of being soft or relaxed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundance or freedom from straitness in one's means or circumstances of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in expressions for an easy state of mind or an untroubled condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ample, unstraitened, easy, pleasant, or plentiful in life or circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to life, a person's condition, or the state of mind expressed by رَخِيُّ البَالِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or part of a thing that has been let loose, let down, or lowered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used, for example, of a loosened veil or curtain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal that runs in the manner called إِرْخَاءٌ, or runs extensively in that manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a horse, mare, she-camel, she-ass, or other beast; its plural is مَرَاخِيُّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Later than, after, or temporally remote from something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction compares the time of one event with the time of another.

Ampleness of life's means or circumstances.

cautions: The Quran occurrence is securely located by QAC at 38:36; historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not independently converted into a modern verse location.
Classical evidence records multiple vocalizations and related derived forms; these variants are kept distinct where their lexical identity or construction differs.
